content.text: The panel title is fixed. Before creating the alert rule, I'll check whether one with this name already exists and whether alerting is healthy.

Both the dashboard and the alert rule exist, and the rule is enabled.

**Data:** The Kibana Sample Data Logs view has 14,074 requests from 1,001 client IPs across 4 hosts. Only three response codes appear: 200 (12,832), 404 (801), and 503 (441). The only 5xx code is 503. Timestamps run from 2026-10-04 to 2026-12-03, so part of the data is in the future relative to today.

**Dashboard:** "EFF-d2653e20 Web logs overview" has five panels, with a time range of now-1y to now+1y so the future-dated data shows up:
- Total requests (metric)
- Unique client IPs (metric)
- Requests by response code (pie, split on `response.keyword`)
- Requests over time (area, date histogram on `timestamp`)
- Average bytes by host (bar, split on `host.keyword`)

I initially titled the time-series panel "Requests over time by response code", but it doesn't split by response code, so I renamed it to "Requests over time".

**Alert rule:** "EFF-d2653e20 5xx spike" is an `.es-query` rule on `kibana_sample_data_logs`, using `timestamp`. It runs every 1m, counts documents where `response.keyword` matches `5*` in a 5-minute window, and fires when the count is greater than 10. It's enabled. Its status is still "pending" because it hasn't run yet.

Since only 441 documents in the whole dataset are 5xx, this rule may rarely fire unless the sample data is refreshed or you add traffic.

I used the Kibana MCP tools for everything. `KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY` isn't visible to my shell, so I didn't call the REST API directly.
